100yen.title: 100-Yen Shops in Japan: 5 Things to Know
100yen.desc: Shopping at a 100-yen shop in Japan? Many items are 100 yen plus tax, so about 110 yen at the register, and some items may cost 300 or 500 yen, or more. You can often find small bags, adapters, umbrellas and snacks. Shopping bags often cost a few yen, and plugs and electronics may be made for Japan, so check the package. Prices vary by store. bow.title: Do You Need to Bow in Japan? 5 Tips for Visitors
bow.desc: Worried about bowing in Japan? Visitors are not expected to bow perfectly; a small nod often works. Say "arigatou gozaimasu" with a smile. Shop staff often bow, and a nod or smile back is a kind reply. Some people may offer a handshake, especially in business, so follow their lead. Being polite matters more than the exact angle. Customs vary by situation. Get the free 1-page Japan Quick Start cheat sheet. #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan

mistakes.title: 5 First-Timer Mistakes in Japan (and How to Avoid Them)
mistakes.desc: First trip to Japan? Avoid these common mistakes: planning to pay by card only (keep some cash as backup), talking loudly or taking calls on local trains, hunting for trash bins (carry your trash until you find a proper bin), tipping automatically (usually unnecessary), and overplanning (leave buffer time for big stations and wrong exits). Rules vary by place. More in JAPAN LIKE A LOCAL, a 13-page PDF guide for first-time visitors ($4.99). #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan
